title: Compatible unit roots and roots of unity on a pointed universal cover
statement: Let $p$ be a positive prime and $E$ a commutative ring of characteristic $p$ with nonempty connected affine spectrum. Fix a geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and let $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ be its pointed universal finite-etale limit cover [lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover]. Put $N_p=\{n>0:(n,p)=1\}$. There exist primitive $\bar\zeta_n\in\Omega$ with $\bar\zeta_m^{m/n}=\bar\zeta_n$ for $n\mid m$ in $N_p$. For any such choice, there are unique sections of the split finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] root-of-unity schemes with those geometric-fibre labels. Their values $\zeta_n\in H$ satisfy $\zeta_n^n=1$, $\zeta_m^{m/n}=\zeta_n$, and $\zeta_n^a-\zeta_n^b$ is a unit whenever $a,b$ are distinct modulo $n$. For any finite family $a_j\in E^\times$, one can choose compatible $\bar b_{j,n}\in\Omega$ with $\bar b_{j,n}^n=s(a_j)$ and $\bar b_{j,m}^{m/n}=\bar b_{j,n}$. The corresponding normalized split sections of $z^n=a_j$ give units $b_{j,n}\in H$ satisfying these same equations. All these sections commute with pointed pullback of $E$ and $H$ and with power maps. Primitive means multiplicative order exactly $n$.

proof.text: Order the private copy of the positive prime-to-p integers by divisibility, with product as common upper bound. At n take the finite subtype of primitive n-th roots in the geometric field. It is nonempty by HasEnoughRootsOfUnity.exists_primitiveRoot: invertibleOfCoprime makes n a unit in E, hence a nonzero element of Ω. For n dividing m the power m/n preserves primitivity by IsPrimitiveRoot.pow. The quotient-chain identity proves functoriality. Apply nonempty_sections_of_finite_inverse_system; no surjectivity hypothesis on transitions is required.

For every scalar a in Ω, use the same inverse index with finite subtype {z : z^n=a}. Finiteness follows by injection into nthRootsFinset, and nonemptiness by IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq. The power transitions and their composition are the elementary exponent identities. The finite inverse-limit theorem supplies compatible scalar roots, also for a=0. Apply this independently to each member of the finite unit family; the empty family is included.

For a unit a and positive n, monic_X_pow_sub_C.finite_adjoinRoot gives finiteness of the root algebra. The proved source helper AdjoinRoot.etale_X_pow_sub_C (the standard-etale calculation audited under lem-sc-kummer-exact) gives etaleness directly, using invertibleOfCoprime for n and the given unit a. Transfer both algebraic properties to Spec with the ring-hom property equivalences.

A geometric root defines an AdjoinRoot.lift homomorphism to Ω, hence a marked point of the finite etale root cover. The existing UniversalCover.toObj section and its proved toObj_hom and pt_toObj equations give a homomorphism from the root algebra into Γ(cover s,top), by the affine correspondence. Its root value satisfies the required equation and evaluation. Its power is a unit, hence it is a unit.

For uniqueness and invertible differences use the following explicit connected-ring calculation. If f(x)=f(y)=0 and f'(x) is a unit v, set q=f/(X-x). Polynomial differentiation gives q(x)=v, and polynomial division gives (y-x)q(y)=0. Write q(y)=v+(y-x)z using sub_dvd_eval_sub. Then e=v^(-1)q(y) is idempotent and e(y-x)=0. Connectedness forces e=0 or 1. If e=1 then y=x; if e=0 then (y-x)(-v^(-1)z)=1. Thus two simple roots are equal or have unit difference. Apply this to X^n-a; its derivative at a unit root is a unit. Equal marked values exclude the unit-difference case. Connectedness of the actual cover is the source connectedSpace_cover instance; connectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem supplies the idempotent criterion.

Choose the uniquely normalized root for each label from step 4. AdjoinRoot.lift gives a homomorphism with that root value and prescribed restriction to E. Every candidate homomorphism sends the quotient root to another normalized root, so step 5 identifies its root value. AdjoinRoot.ringHom_ext identifies the entire homomorphism. This proves the asserted unique existence.

For n dividing m, the (m/n)-th power of the normalized m-th root satisfies the n-th root equation because (m/n)n=m, and its evaluation is the prescribed powered label. Step 5 proves the order compatibility. The same calculation with the k-th power and a^k proves the second power identity. For primitive labels, equality of two root powers would imply equality of the geometric powers; reduce exponents modulo n and apply IsPrimitiveRoot.pow_inj. The roots are distinct, so step 5 proves their difference is a unit.

Given any pointed ring maps in the final clause, the base equation makes the image of the chosen root an n-th root of f(a); the point equation gives its transported label. Apply step 5 on the primed cover to compare this image with b. The already established power identities and the scalar families from step 2 supply all remaining clauses.

f : AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial E) ^ n.val - Polynomial.C (a : E)) →+* pointedCoverRing s, (∀ e : E, f (AdjoinRoot.of _ e) = pointedCoverBase s e) ∧ pointedCoverEval s (f (AdjoinRoot.root _)) = c.val) ∧ (∀ (a : Eˣ) (n m : TameRootOrder p) (_h : n.val ∣ m.val) (c : {c : Ω // c ^ m.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom (a : E)}) (d : {d : Ω // d ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom (a : E)}), c.val ^ (m.val / n.val) = d.val → root a m c ^ (m.val / n.val) = root a n d) ∧ (∀ (a : Eˣ) (n : TameRootOrder p) (k : ℕ) (c : {c : Ω // c ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom (a : E)}) (d : {d : Ω // d ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom ((a ^ k : Eˣ) : E)}), c.val ^ k = d.val → root a n c ^ k = root (a ^ k) n d) ∧ (∀ (n : TameRootOrder p) (c : {c : Ω // c ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom ((1 : Eˣ) : E)}), IsPrimitiveRoot c.val n.val → ∀ a b : ℕ, a % n.val ≠ b % n.val → IsUnit (root 1 n c ^ a - root 1 n c ^ b)) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → Eˣ), ∃ b : Fin r → TameRootOrder p → Ω, (∀ j n, b j n ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom (a j : E)) ∧ ∀ j n m, n.val ∣ m.val → b j m ^ (m.val / n.val) = b j n) ∧ (∀ {E' Ω' : Type u} [CommRing E'] [CharP E' p] [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of E'))] [Field Ω'] [IsAlgClosed Ω'] (s' : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Spec (.of E')) (f : E →+* E') (ι : Ω →+* Ω') (g : pointedCoverRing s →+* pointedCoverRing s') (_hbase : g.comp (pointedCoverBase s) = (pointedCoverBase s').comp f) (_hpoint : (pointedCoverEval s').comp g = ι.comp (pointedCoverEval s)) (a : Eˣ) (n : TameRootOrder p) (c : {c : Ω // c ^ n.val = (Spec.homEquiv s).hom (a : E)}) (b : pointedCoverRing s'), b ^ n.val = pointedCoverBase s' (f (a : E)) → pointedCoverEval s' b = ι c.val → g (root a n c) = b)
lean.note: Uses the actual UniversalCover limit, its global section ring and marked point. Root-scheme sections are ring homomorphisms from the explicit AdjoinRoot algebra, with their base restriction and geometric label fixed; uniqueness includes the entire section. Universal normalized lifting renders every compatible primitive/unit-label choice. Pointed pullback is the induced map on the actual coordinate rings, characterized by the base and marked-point squares. TameRootOrder is reused from its landed owning node.
